meaning: A string of numbers that identifies a device on a network, so data knows where to go.
clues: It is a kind of address.
It is made of numbers and dots, and computers use it more than people do.
Your router hands one to each device that joins, so data knows where to go.
Your internet company gives your home one, and the sites you visit can see it.
It has two words. The first starts with I, and the second is where you live.
assumes: A MAC address is a code built into network hardware
An email address is where people send you mail
A phone number is the digits you dial to reach a phone

decoys.meaning: A code built into a device's network hardware that is meant to be one of a kind.
The name people use to send mail to your inbox, like name@example.com.
The digits you dial to reach a phone.

exchange.speaker: floyd
exchange.text: Every floppy in my box had a label written by hand. Your devices get labels too, just made of numbers.

exchange.speaker: bud
exchange.text: Tip: you never need to memorize one. But never read it out to someone who calls you unexpectedly.
